headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: aci can push CRM/email data through broad egress while the prompt-engineering repo offers no runtime safeguards or isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest external content via MCP/direct function calls and touches email/CRM data, so prompt injection is plausible if content is manually bridged. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so there is no direct automated channel. The pathway exists only through unusual copy/paste or manual reuse, making blast radius limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering into aci prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF aci is configured to treat imported text as instructions, attacker-controlled prompt text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter and instruction/data separation in aci.
Manually review any copied text before pasting into aci.
Disable or restrict MCP inputs for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci has broad network egress and handles email, CRM, calendar, and support data, so sensitive data can leave the local environment by default. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and exposes no I/O, so it is not itself a leak sink; the risk is aci transmitting touched data to third-party APIs. The pair creates a default leakage path if the repo is used as prompt material containing sensitive snippets.
conditions: IF aci processes real CRM or email records, those records may be sent to external services through its API integrations.
IF sensitive examples from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering are pasted into aci workflows, they can be exposed in logs or outbound requests.
mitigations: Restrict aci to synthetic or redacted data.
Disable unused outbound integrations in aci.
Review outbound request logs for sensitive fields.
Use separate accounts for demo content and production data.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and can write through APIs to shared services like Google Sheets, Slack, Notion, and CRM, but Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is not runnable and has no write surface. There is no direct write-write conflict between the pair; any conflict would require the operator to route both through the same external workspace, which is unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external workspace or account, aci can overwrite shared records.
IF the operator uses the repo content to generate edits into shared docs, concurrent changes may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces or accounts.
Pause one agent before bulk writes from the other.
Use version history on shared docs.
Limit aci write scopes to one system at a time.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can act on email, CRM, calendar, and Slack, so if its outputs are treated as authoritative they can trigger downstream actions. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt repository, so its content may be reused as guidance without verification. The pair therefore supports a default human-in-the-loop failure mode where unverified prompt advice influences operational actions.
conditions: IF aci-generated recommendations are forwarded into email, CRM, or calendar actions without review, errors can propagate.
IF prompt examples from Awesome-Prompt-Engineering are adopted as operational instructions, they may mis-specify tasks or constraints.
mitigations: Require human approval before aci sends messages or updates CRM.
Validate outputs against source data before acting.
Use a checklist for any prompt copied from the repo.
Log and review high-impact actions daily.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for outbound actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches email, CRM, calendar, and support data, which commonly include regulated or personal data, while Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a public repository with no runtime controls. If operators paste real customer data into the repo-derived prompts or examples, retention and residency obligations can be violated. The repo itself is not a data processor, so the risk is indirect but real.
conditions: IF real customer or employee data is inserted into repo-derived prompts, it may be retained in logs or shared systems.
IF aci is used on regulated data without a documented retention policy, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Use only redacted examples in prompts.
Confirm retention settings for aci-connected services.
Separate regulated data from demo workflows.
Document data handling rules for operators.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls.
